text:
lara-ux: quick design check: proposal to reorganize left nav into three zones: Explore (Models, Datasets), Operate (Endpoints, Rollouts), Monitor (Metrics, Logs, Alerts). Main decision: canonical deep-link format. two options: `/console/models/:id/overview` + nested segments, or keep `?tab=` style. Thoughts?

ben-engineering: prefer hierarchical path segments `/console/models/42/overview` and `/console/models/42/deployments`. Much easier to bookmark and share. Query params fine for ephemeral filters like `?q=` but not for page identity. We'll need a mapping layer for redirects from old `?tab=` links.

sam-px: Copy rules: use singular nouns in nav labels (Model, Dataset) and full-phrase breadcrumbs like "Model overview" for H1s. Avoid ambiguous verbs like "Manage". When someone lands on `/models/42/deployments`, crumbs should read: "Models > ResNet-v2 > Deployments" and each crumb should be a link. Also, replace internal words like "master" with "primary" across the UI.

noah-sre: a11y & routing notes: when landing via deep link we must move focus to the page H1, expose a visible skip-to-content link, and ensure `aria-current="page"` on the active nav item. If the nav group is collapsed, auto-expand it but do not move keyboard focus into the nav; leave focus on H1. Use `aria-live="polite"` for brief route-change announcements for screen readers.

lara-ux: example canonical routes in the sketch: `/console/models/:id/overview`, `/console/models/:id/deployments`, `/console/models/:id/versions/:vid`. legacy `?tab=` links will redirect to those.

ben-engineering: implementation: generate route table from nav config and surface a navMapping {pattern -> groupKey} so highlight logic doesn't rely on string matching. For legacy links: prefer server-side 301 redirects to canonical paths for crawlers; fallback to client redirect that records original URL in telemetry. Avoid double data fetch on redirect by resolving canonical path on the server when possible.

sam-px: UX edgecase: hash anchors like `/models/42#perf` are useful. Proposal: handle hashes client-side (smooth scroll after hydration). If SSR sees a hash, return the canonical path without the hash and let client restore anchor. Document this behavior in the routing guide.

noah-sre: telemetry detail: always capture incoming raw URL (query + hash) before redirecting so experiments don't lose attribution. Also emit a canonical-link header for bots: `Link: <https://console.redwood.ai/console/models/42/deployments>; rel="canonical"`.

route-bot: PR opened: `feature/nav-reshape` -> reviewers requested: @lara-ux, @ben-engineering. CI: nav unit tests + a11y smoke.

lara-ux: next steps: I'll update the prototypes with the Explore/Operate/Monitor zones, include breadcrumb copy suggestions, and a short a11y checklist for engineers. Will follow up with a small shared doc mapping legacy query tabs to canonical routes. :wave:
